suite.name: RAG Pipeline Evaluation Suite v1
suite.description: Golden dataset for evaluating RAG retrieval and RAGAS metrics against ingested docs

questions.question: What is EvalForge and what does it benchmark?
questions.golden_answer: EvalForge is an enterprise AI evaluation and benchmarking platform designed to test LLMs and RAG pipelines against golden datasets, measuring metrics such as hallucination rate, latency, and cost.

questions.question: What core technologies make up the backend of EvalForge?
questions.golden_answer: The EvalForge backend is built using FastAPI on Python 3.11+, asynchronous SQLAlchemy 2.0 with PostgreSQL, Celery worker queue with Redis broker, and Chroma vector store.

questions.question: How does Celery process evaluation tasks in EvalForge?
questions.golden_answer: Celery runs background worker processes powered by a Redis broker to execute evaluation batches asynchronously without blocking FastAPI HTTP API routes.

questions.question: What vector store is used for local RAG evaluations in EvalForge and why?
questions.golden_answer: EvalForge uses ChromaDB as its local vector store because it requires no external cloud service and persists document embeddings locally.

questions.question: What embedding model is used by default in EvalForge's RAG engine?
questions.golden_answer: EvalForge uses the sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model for local document embedding and semantic retrieval.

questions.question: What text splitter configuration is used for document chunking in EvalForge?
questions.golden_answer: Document chunking uses RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter configured with a chunk size of 500 characters and a chunk overlap of 50 characters.

questions.question: What document formats does the EvalForge RAG pipeline ingest?
questions.golden_answer: The RAG pipeline ingests Markdown (.md) and PDF (.pdf) document files located in the /docs directory.

questions.question: Explain Faithfulness in the context of RAGAS metrics.
questions.golden_answer: Faithfulness evaluates whether all statements in the generated response are strictly grounded in the retrieved context chunks, preventing hallucinations and unauthorized extrapolation.

questions.question: Explain Answer Relevance in RAGAS metrics.
questions.golden_answer: Answer Relevance measures how directly and completely the generated response addresses the user's prompt without introducing off-topic or extraneous information.

questions.question: Explain Context Precision in RAGAS metrics.
questions.golden_answer: Context Precision measures the retrieval quality of the vector store by calculating Average Precision at rank K (AP@k) to ensure the most relevant context chunks are ranked at the top.

questions.question: What are the two evaluation target types supported by EvalForge?
questions.golden_answer: EvalForge supports two evaluation target types: 'raw_llm' for direct LLM output benchmarking and 'rag' for RAG pipeline evaluation with Chroma retrieval and RAGAS metrics.

questions.question: What quality gate thresholds does EvalForge enforce?
questions.golden_answer: EvalForge enforces quality gates requiring a minimum pass rate of 80%, a maximum hallucination rate of 15%, and a maximum p95 latency of 10,000 milliseconds.

questions.question: Can EvalForge benchmark custom deployed LLM endpoints?
questions.golden_answer: Yes, EvalForge supports custom endpoint_url overrides per evaluation run, allowing users to target any local or deployed Ollama-compatible LLM endpoint.

questions.question: How are evaluation results stored in PostgreSQL?
questions.golden_answer: Evaluation results are stored in PostgreSQL using the eval_results schema with JSONB columns for flexible scoring metadata and retrieved context persistence.

questions.question: What happens if the LLM judge call fails during RAGAS metric evaluation?
questions.golden_answer: If the LLM judge fails or times out, EvalForge uses deterministic local NLP fallback heuristics based on n-gram context grounding and TF-IDF similarity.

questions.question: How do you trigger a RAG evaluation run via the EvalForge CLI?
questions.golden_answer: You can trigger a RAG evaluation run using the EvalForge CLI with the command: evalforge test --target-type rag --ollama-model phi4
